## Natural history notes

A tiny concealer moth characterized by narrow grayish-brown to tan wings with subtle mottled markings, making the adult easy to overlook on bark or dried vegetation. In Florida, it is found in oak woodlands, hammocks, pine-oak forests, parks, yards, and other habitats where acorns and leaf litter are available. The caterpillars feed concealed in acorns, seeds, or related plant material, helping break down fallen oak resources while also serving as prey for spiders, birds, parasitoid wasps, and other insect-eating animals.
